# LOCAL-4: Second tutorial screen ("how to use the app")

## Context / findings
- `main` (and this branch, currently identical to it) has **no tutorial/onboarding code and no navigation library at all**. `MainActivity` composes `HomeScreen()` directly (`app/src/main/java/com/example/myapplication/MainActivity.kt`).
- This ticket is part of a series (LOCAL-3 "first screen", LOCAL-4 "second screen" — this one, LOCAL-5 "third screen", LOCAL-6 "fourth screen"). None of the sibling screens exist in git history yet (their branches only contain stale planning artifacts from an unrelated ticket), so there is no screen 1 to build on top of and no established navigation graph to plug into.
- An unmerged, unrelated-ticket branch (`gerardosuarez/local-5-local-5-onboarding-scientific-interest-s`, a *different* LOCAL-5 for interest-selection onboarding — not the tutorial-series LOCAL-5) previously prototyped a 3-screen onboarding flow with Navigation-Compose 2.8.5. It's a useful style reference but not something to depend on or merge from.
- The app itself (`HomeScreen.kt`) is a TikTok-style vertical-swipe feed of short science videos with a right-hand action rail (like / comment / share) and a top Following/For You tab row.

## Assumptions (no navigation framework exists yet, and this ticket is scoped to *one screen* of a 4-part series)
1. This ticket only requires **building the screen itself**, not a full navigation graph. Since screens 1/3/4 are separate tickets likely being built independently, the screen will be self-contained and take `onNext`/`onSkip`/`onBack` callback lambdas so it can be wired into whichever navigation solution a later integration ticket introduces (Navigation Compose or Navigation3 — the codebase has no precedent for either yet). This avoids taking an irreversible dependency decision that isn't this ticket's job.
2. Content: since screen 1 (welcome/intro) isn't built yet, screen 2 is assumed to be the first *substantive* instructional step: **"Swipe to explore"** — teaching the user the app's core interaction (vertical swipe between videos), mirroring `HomeScreen`'s actual `VerticalPager` behavior. This keeps the tutorial grounded in a real, verifiable app feature rather than invented generic content.
3. Follows the existing stateless-screen convention (`WelcomeScreen`-style from the onboarding reference branch, and the stateful/stateless split used in `HomeScreen.kt`): no ViewModel needed since there's no async data or business state, just static instructional content — matches project convention of only adding a ViewModel when there's real state/logic (see `HomeViewModel`).
4. Not wiring this screen into `MainActivity` / a nav graph, since none exists — it will be a standalone, previewable, testable Composable ready for integration.

## Files to add
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/myapplication/tutorial/SwipeToExploreScreen.kt`
  - `@Composable fun SwipeToExploreScreen(step: Int = 2, totalSteps: Int = 4, onNext: () -> Unit = {}, onSkip: () -> Unit = {})`
  - Layout (Material3 stock components only, matching project convention — no custom design-system components exist to reuse):
    - Full-bleed dark background `Box` (`Color.Black`, consistent with `HomeScreen`'s dark TikTok-style aesthetic) via `Modifier.fillMaxSize().background(...)`.
    - Centered illustrative content: a large emoji/icon (e.g. "⬆️") + headline `Text` ("Swipe to explore") + supporting body `Text` ("Swipe up or down to move between videos, just like your favorite feed.") using `MaterialTheme.typography`.
    - Step indicator: a row of small dots (`Box` circles) reflecting `step`/`totalSteps`, current step highlighted — simple inline composable, no external pager-indicator dependency.
    - Bottom action row: `TextButton` "Skip" (`onSkip`) and `Button` "Next" (`onNext`), laid out with `Row` + `Arrangement.SpaceBetween`, `navigationBarsPadding()`.
    - `Modifier.testTag(...)` on the headline, Next button, and Skip button (`"tutorial_step2_headline"`, `"tutorial_step2_next"`, `"tutorial_step2_skip"`) to support future Compose UI testing, matching the convention observed in the onboarding reference branch.
  - `@Preview(showBackground = true, backgroundColor = 0xFF1A1A2E)` wrapping content in `MyApplicationTheme { SwipeToExploreScreen() }`, matching `HomeScreenPreview` convention.

## Testing
- `app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/myapplication/tutorial/SwipeToExploreScreenTest.kt`
  - `@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)`, `createComposeRule()` (no Activity dependency needed since the screen takes no ViewModel/Activity context).
  - Assert headline text and both buttons are displayed (`onNodeWithTag(...).assertIsDisplayed()`).
  - Click "Next" → assert `onNext` lambda invoked (via a local boolean flag).
  - Click "Skip" → assert `onSkip` lambda invoked.
  - Matches the `OnboardingHappyPathTest`-style pattern seen in the reference branch (Compose UI test + testTags), adapted since this screen has no Activity/nav dependency to test against.
- No unit test needed — there's no ViewModel/business logic in this screen, consistent with why `WelcomeScreen` (the closest precedent) also had no accompanying unit test.

## Out of scope (left to future/integration tickets)
- Wiring `SwipeToExploreScreen` into an actual navigation graph or `MainActivity` — no nav library exists in the project yet, and introducing one is a bigger decision (Navigation Compose vs. Navigation3) that spans all 4 tutorial screens, not just this one.
- Building screen 1 (welcome/intro), which this screen would logically follow — that's LOCAL-3.
- Persisting "tutorial seen" state (e.g. DataStore) — no such mechanism exists yet and isn't needed to just render this screen.
